Also Knapper 2006, 10.1182/blood-2006-04-015560 (verified, PMID 16857985): responses only 'where the presence of sustained FLT3-inhibitory drug levels' - an abstract-level warning about inconsistent lestaurtinib exposure five years before the phase 3.

dose: Levis 2006 (full text) is the first published exposure miss: IC50 ~2 nM in medium vs ~700 nM in plasma, 'an approximately 300-fold difference in potency ... in medium compared with plasma' (AGP binding), 85% PIA needing 'roughly 5 uM'. That 5 uM trough target is the prediction Sato 2011 says failed ('we had predicted that trough levels of 5 uM in vivo would be sufficient'). Magnitude for 2006 = off_by_>5x; Sato's in-vitro FL shift = off_by_2-5x (Table 2: lestaurtinib 3.3->6.8 nM, AC220 0.38->1.3 nM).

efficacy: once the 2011 contra is withdrawn, the first efficacy `same` on the same FLT3-ITD cell-line/mouse family is RATIFY - midostaurin + chemotherapy improved OS in FLT3-mutated AML, Stone 2017 NEJM, PMID 28644114, doi 10.1056/NEJMoa1614359 (resolved by title search; abstract not fetched; preclinical model Weisberg 2002 Cancer Cell Ba/F3-FLT3-ITD cells + mouse, DOI not verified; registry not looked up). Then ADMIRAL 2019 (Perl 2019, 10.1056/NEJMoa1902688 verified, PMID 31665578; Mori 2017 MV4-11/MOLM-13 xenografts, 10.1007/s10637-017-0470-z verified, PMID 28516360) is a second same, not a status change.

dose (judgement claims): Cortes 2013 (10.1200/JCO.2013.48.8783 verified, PMID 24002496) and Perl 2017 (10.1016/S1470-2045(17)30416-3 verified, PMID 28645776) say what the draft says, but for quizartinib the PIA showed complete inhibition at every dose and the dose was set by QT (DLT grade 3 QT, MTD 200 mg) - PIA did not 'predict the dose'. Whether the FDA Xospata/Vanflyta clinical-pharmacology reviews make a model-vs-patient exposure comparison (model_filed) was not checked.
safety: registry for the Sexauer cohort is NCT00989261 (AC220-002, phase 2) - the draft says not identified. Quizartinib QT/hERG: FDA Vanflyta nonclinical review not checked here (budget).

registry: NCT00079482 confirmed completed, no results posted (has_results false); ClinicalTrials.gov lists it as PHASE2 and Levis 2011 never calls it phase 3 ('Cephalon 204 trial'); the draft's 'phase 3' wording is loose.
rule_questions: Model switch (Q1): under the brief a switch of the class's relied-on model opens a new status - status is 'of the BEST model ... as of a year' and contra is 'the model predicted wrongly'; the draft already applies this in engagement (2002 cells -> 2006 PIA). But no switch happened in the dose cell: the PIA-calibrated 5 uM trough target was already lestaurtinib's dose model (Smith 2004, Levis 2006; Sato 2011: 'we had predicted that trough levels of 5 uM in vivo would be sufficient') and it missed in relapsed patients, so the PIA-guided gilteritinib dose is the same model's later record and the override applies: the cell stays red. The brief should state explicitly whether contra is per-model or per-cell; the draft's reason ('a contra is not lifted') is the wrong reason for the right answer.

Is a patient-plasma-on-cells assay (PIA) a 'model' for the atlas or the patient-side measurement? It is both. I accepted it as the cell model's engagement read-out for `same` (as the draft did) but not as something that can 'flag' a drug for `neg`: in Levis 2011 it is a within-trial PD read-out reported with the outcome, not a prior prediction.

Efficacy (Q2): a negative trial whose authors state the efficacy hypothesis was not tested (58% target inhibition; inhibited patients remitted more) - contra or no change? Rules 1-2 (the source must make the comparison; comparison_stated is false) give no change and put the failure in dose; the ad-amyloid precedent (trial failure = contra, no explicit comparison in Doody 2013) pulls the other way. I applied rules 1-2.

`neg` (Q3): the brief does not say the flag must precede the failure or must come from the model rather than a within-trial PD assay. I applied both; without them every negative trial with a PD correlate becomes `neg`.

Scaling misses: a ~300-fold protein-binding shift (Levis 2006) and a 2-4x FL shift (Sato 2011) are scored contra under the current rules by the draft's own logic (source_calls_it = scaling). The fact fields anticipate re-scoring; a rule decision on whether 'scaling' is a miss is needed and would move the dose cell.
